Task 3 Identify potential customers and develop evaluation plan: The SST technology can facilitate the DER participation in the markets to provide grid services which would provide numerous sources of value to different stakeholders. The value could be in the form of improved grid control (volt/VAR control, storage), better visibility as a distributed sensor, synthetic inertia etc. Thus, the SST technology can benefit utilities, DER aggregators, balancing authorities etc. This task identifies the potential customers of the SST technology. An evaluation plan will be developed by NREL team to quantify the incremental value of the SST to these customers. The simulation scenarios will be designed by NREL team to extract the data required for this evaluation. Estimated completion: 9 months from project start. The MV SSTs can provide benefits not only to the stakeholders such as utilities and DER developers/aggregators, but also to the balancing authorities and the customers. Some of the benefits to potential stakeholders and customers have been discussed here. Benefits to stakeholders 1. Utilities SSTs can help the utilities with grid stability and reliability. SSTs can provide voltage and frequency regulation, and enable better integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind, into the grid. SSTs can potentially reduce the need for maintenance and repairs, as they have fewer moving parts and are more durable than traditional transformers. 2.
